videos.description:
How to clean bird feeders the easy way! Fall is the best time to clean your bird feeders since birds are molting and foraging naturally. Skip the gimmicky feeder cleaners: all you need is Dawn dish soap, very hot water, a stiff scrub brush, a Scrub Daddy, and a mascara wand for small ports. For extra dirty feeders, soak in a 1:10 bleach to water solution and rinse well. Dry completely before refilling for fall and winter. 🧼🐦🍂

videos.title: Where do goldfinches go in fall? Nowhere! American goldfinches molt twice a year, and in October the
videos.description:
Where do goldfinches go in fall? Nowhere! American goldfinches molt twice a year, and in October the bright yellow males fade to a duller winter plumage that looks a lot like the females. This camouflage helps them stay safe, but it makes them easy to miss at your bird feeder.

Bird feeding tips for fall goldfinches: keep your feeders out, use a sock feeder with Nyjer (thistle) seed for small numbers, and size up your feeder for larger flocks. 🐦💛

videos.description:
Late season hummingbirds still visiting in October! If you’re seeing hummingbirds after early October, keep your hummingbird feeder up. Bring it in, give it a quick wash, and refill with fresh Petal Potion nectar to fuel late migrating hummingbirds on their trip south. Keeping feeders up in fall does not delay migration.

Plus a birthday shoutout to Crinda’s husband and a big thank you to our community for the support after our recent flood. A strong fall finish means a great spring ahead! 🐦🌺

videos.description:
Late hummingbird sighting in October! Crinda returned home on October 10th after a week and a half away and found a hummingbird visiting the backyard feeders. Seeing a hummingbird after the first week of October is rare, so the feeders were washed and refilled with fresh nectar to help this late migrant rest and refuel before continuing its fall migration.

Hummingbird feeder tip: keep your feeders up until mid-October to support late-migrating hummingbirds. 🐦💚

videos.description:
Meet the Witches Brew bird seed blend, our October Halloween special at For The Wild Birds! 🎃 This blend is designed to give migrating birds a big energy boost for cold fall nights.

Ingredients include black oil sunflower, striped sunflower, sunflower hearts, peanut pickouts, mixed nuts, white and golden safflower, flax seed, canary seed, pumpkin seeds, cherries, apricots, apples, raisins, cranberries, and berry suet blend nuggets.

High-fat seeds, nuts, and suet help birds stay warm overnight, while dried fruit attracts fruit-loving species like bluebirds, robins, and mockingbirds. Available through the end of October, with a new blend coming in November!
